task.description:
HARD GATE on CODE-DESIGNER's scoping-decision artefact at lib/letflow/design/iss0438-entity-subsystem-scoping.md. This is NOT a normal implementation-design gate (there is no code yet to check for correctness) -- you are validating that the DECISION and its documented consequences are COMPLETE and UNAMBIGUOUS against all 7 of ISS-0438's acceptance criteria, and that the reasoning is actually grounded in the real source files rather than asserted. Read docs/issues/ISS-0438.yaml in full for the 7 AC text (quoted in step-01's own task.description if you want it inline, but read the issue file directly -- it is the authoritative statement). Independently re-derive your verdict; do not accept CODE-DESIGNER's own claim of completeness on trust (core-directives.md, 'Every producing step has a validating step' -- a validator that only reads the producer's result.summary has not validated anything).

Specifically check:
1. AC1: does the artefact state a clear, unambiguous port-vs-defer decision? Not 'it depends' or a menu of options presented as the decision.
2. AC2 (if in-scope recommended): is the stage/slice breakdown concrete enough that REQ-ANALYST could draft real REQ-xxx entries without re-reading R-Co source? Spot-check at least one of the claimed R-Co file/line facts yourself against the actual R-Co source at c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\R-Co\src\entities\ -- do not trust the artefact's own citations blindly.
3. AC3 (if out-of-scope recommended): does it name the exact router.ex edit and the decision-record path (docs/migration/decisions/0018-*.md)?
4. AC4: is the EventStore.Registry relationship answered by actually reading lib/letflow/event_store/registry.ex's real public interface (register_type/2, validate_payload/3, get_type/2) rather than asserting compatibility abstractly? Verify the claim yourself by opening that file.
5. AC5: is the Repository/ArtifactKind relationship answered against the REAL lib/letflow/repository.ex and its ArtifactKind value-list mechanism? If the artefact claims ArtifactKind needs extending, verify that claim by reading lib/letflow/repository/artifact_kind.ex (or wherever that module actually lives -- find it) and checking its current value list yourself.
6. AC6: does the artefact correctly state the ISS-0439 sequencing relationship, consistent with ISS-0439's own already-recorded text (read docs/issues/ISS-0439.yaml), and does it correctly NOT resolve or reopen ISS-0439?
7. AC7: confirm literally zero implementation code appears -- no Elixir function bodies, no literal Ecto schema field definitions. Sketch-level module/boundary mentions are fine; field-by-field schemas are not.

If ANY check fails, FAIL with the specific gap named per acceptance criterion (validator-fail example shape in HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md). If all pass, PASS and state what you independently re-derived and how (validator-pass example shape).
acceptance_criteria: Every one of ISS-0438's 7 acceptance criteria is checked individually against the artefact, not impressionistically

At least one of CODE-DESIGNER's factual claims about the real Letflow codebase (EventStore.Registry's interface, or ArtifactKind's current value list) is independently verified by opening the actual file, not accepted from the artefact's own citation
At least one of CODE-DESIGNER's factual claims about R-Co's source (a file size, a line count, a described mechanism) is spot-checked against the real R-Co source
The verdict is PASS or FAIL, never a soft 'looks reasonable'
A FAIL names the specific unmet AC and the specific gap, not a general impression
